title: Roy Fielding's Dissertation and the Origin of REST (2000)
explainer: In his 2000 UC Irvine PhD dissertation, Roy Fielding named and formalized "Representational State Transfer" by distilling the architectural constraints already implicit in how the web worked, rather than inventing a new protocol from scratch. Fielding helped write the HTTP/1.1 specification around the same time, which is why REST's rules about resources, a uniform interface, and statelessness map so directly onto HTTP verbs and status codes. Knowing REST was a description of an existing success, not a fresh invention, explains why "RESTful" API design borrows the web's own vocabulary instead of defining its own.

resources.title: Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures, Chapter 5: Representational State Transfer (REST)
